item.title: Why the United States and Iran Keep Fighting While They Negotiate
item.description: What looks like escalation may actually be bargaining. Understanding that changes how we should read the U.S.-Iran conflict.

item.title: Will the U.S.-Saudi Nuclear Deal Proceed?
item.description: President Trump's last-minute link between the U.S.-Saudi nuclear agreement and Israel normalization injects new uncertainty into an already contentious deal.

item.title: How the U.S. Can Survive a Large-Scale AI Cyberattack
item.description: Advances in offensive AI cyber capabilities are threatening U.S. cybersecurity. The U.S. must improve its whole-of-society cyber readiness through enhancing its partnerships and communication before a major AI cyber-attack occurs.

item.title: Detour Dividends: How Syrian Airspace Benefits from the Iran War
item.description: This installment of Charting the Middle East spotlights the unlikely positive implications of flight disruptions for Syria in wake of the Iran war.

item.title: AI Strategies and the Informal Economy: Africa’s Job Creation Test
item.description: African nations have implemented AI strategies that focus on their formal sectors, leaving the informal economy behind.

item.title: What Do the Election Security Documents Say About Chinese Interference in U.S. Elections?
item.description: The biggest takeaway from the declassified intelligence isn't a cover-up—it's how intelligence analysis actually works. Healthy disagreement, documented dissent, and rigorous debate are signs of a strong intelligence community, not a broken one.

item.title: Tracking Global Compulsory Licensing Trends in Biopharmaceuticals
item.description: From HIV/AIDS to Covid-19, global health emergencies have revived calls for compulsory licensing. But history shows that innovation, technology transfer, and manufacturing capacity—not patent waivers alone—drive access to lifesaving medicines.

item.title: Section 232 Explained
item.description: In this week's column, Bill Reinsch explains how Section 232 national security investigations have become popular trade tool of the Trump administration, arguing that while some tariffs are difficult to justify, recent decisions suggest a more selective approach to their use.

item.title: Charting a New Course: Countering China's Dominance in Global Shipbuilding
item.description: China has developed the largest shipbuilding industry in recent history and now uses it as an instrument of national power. It is key to Beijing's ambitions to displace the United States as the preeminent power in the Asia-Pacific and project power far from China’s shores.
